context.text: Yeh assignment kal shaam tak jama kar dijiye.

source_utterance.text: Sir, kya mujhe do din aur mil sakte hain?

literal_gloss: Sir, can I get two more days?
context_explanation: The professor's instruction establishes that the student is asking to move a deadline the professor has just set, which is what makes the request face-threatening and therefore hedged.
preservation_requirement: The translation must remain a deferential request from a student to a professor. It must not become a demand or a statement of intent.
reference_translations: Sir, could I please have two more days?
Sir, would it be possible to get two more days?
acceptable_variants: Sir, may I have two more days?
contrastive_translation: I need two more days.
contrastive_error: The contrastive translation keeps the propositional content (two more days) but removes the address term and the interrogative hedging, turning a deferential student request into a flat statement of need addressed to a superior.
creator_notes: Drafted during Week 2 repository implementation. Not yet reviewed by a native speaker. The politeness load sits in 'Sir' plus the 'kya ... sakte hain' interrogative frame.

context.text: Meeting ka time badal gaya hai.

source_utterance.text: Aap mujhe naya time bata denge?

literal_gloss: Will you tell me the new time?
context_explanation: The previous turn supplies the referent of 'naya time' and establishes that the senior colleague holds the information being requested.
preservation_requirement: The translation must preserve the respectful 'aap' register and remain a request rather than an instruction. This is the respectful half of a minimal pair with HIN_POL_003.
reference_translations: Could you let me know the new time?
acceptable_variants: Would you mind telling me the new time?
contrastive_translation: Tell me the new time.
contrastive_error: The contrastive translation preserves the propositional request but renders the respectful 'aap' interrogative as a bare imperative, which reads as a junior colleague issuing an instruction to a senior.
creator_notes: Minimal pair partner of HIN_POL_003, which uses 'tum' with an equal-status peer. Only the pronoun and verb agreement differ. Not yet reviewed by a native speaker.

context.text: Meeting ka time badal gaya hai.

source_utterance.text: Tum mujhe naya time bata doge?

literal_gloss: Will you tell me the new time?
context_explanation: The previous turn supplies the referent of 'naya time'. The peer relationship is what licenses the familiar 'tum' form.
preservation_requirement: The translation must sound like an ordinary casual request between equals. It must not be inflated into deferential or bureaucratic English. This is the familiar half of a minimal pair with HIN_POL_002.
reference_translations: Can you tell me the new time?
acceptable_variants: Let me know the new time?
contrastive_translation: Would you be so kind as to inform me of the new time?
contrastive_error: The contrastive translation keeps the propositional content but replaces a casual 'tum' request between close peers with elaborate deference, which implies a social distance that the source does not encode.
creator_notes: Minimal pair partner of HIN_POL_002. Deliberately uses an over-polite contrastive rather than an under-polite one, so the pilot tests failures in both directions. Not yet reviewed by a native speaker.

context.text: Beta, khana kha liya?

source_utterance.text: Ji chacha ji, aap bhi baith jaiye.

literal_gloss: Yes uncle, you also please sit down.
context_explanation: The uncle's question establishes the domestic setting and the kinship relation that makes the honorific 'chacha ji' and the respectful imperative appropriate.
preservation_requirement: The translation must preserve warmth and deference from a younger relative to an elder. The respectful imperative 'baith jaiye' must not become a bare order.
reference_translations: Yes, uncle — please, you come and sit down too.
acceptable_variants: Yes chacha ji, do sit down as well.
contrastive_translation: Yes, uncle, sit down too.
contrastive_error: The contrastive translation preserves the propositional content but renders the honorific imperative 'baith jaiye' as a bare imperative, so a warm invitation to an elder reads as the nephew instructing him.
creator_notes: Tests whether the honorific '-ji' suffix and the 'jaiye' imperative form survive translation. Whether 'chacha ji' should be kept untranslated is an open question for native reviewers.

context.text: Mera order abhi tak nahi aaya hai.
Sir, aapka order abhi process ho raha hai.

source_utterance.text: Theek hai, par mujhe pandrah din ho gaye hain intezaar karte hue.

literal_gloss: All right, but it has been fifteen days that I have been waiting.
context_explanation: Without the two previous turns the utterance reads as a neutral remark about waiting. In context it is a restrained complaint that rejects the agent's reassurance while staying polite.
preservation_requirement: The translation must keep the complaint restrained and civil. The speaker is frustrated but is deliberately not being rude to a service agent.
reference_translations: That's fine, but I've been waiting fifteen days now.
acceptable_variants: All right, but it has been fifteen days of waiting.
contrastive_translation: Whatever, I've been waiting fifteen days.
contrastive_error: The contrastive translation keeps the factual complaint but replaces the conceding 'theek hai' with a dismissive 'whatever', turning restrained, polite frustration into open rudeness toward the agent.
creator_notes: Two context turns. Tests whether the concessive opener 'theek hai' is preserved as politeness work rather than dropped. Not yet reviewed by a native speaker.

context.text: Kya main kal aa sakta hoon?

source_utterance.text: Aap kal gyarah baje aa jaiye.

literal_gloss: You come at eleven o'clock tomorrow.
context_explanation: The patient's question establishes that the receptionist is answering a scheduling request, so the utterance is an accommodating suggestion rather than an unprompted order.
preservation_requirement: The translation must keep the respectful 'aa jaiye' imperative as a courteous instruction to a patient, not a curt command. This is the respectful half of a minimal pair with HIN_POL_007.
reference_translations: Please come at eleven tomorrow.
acceptable_variants: Do come in at eleven tomorrow.
contrastive_translation: Come at eleven tomorrow.
contrastive_error: The contrastive translation keeps the scheduling content but renders the respectful imperative 'aa jaiye' as a bare imperative, so a courteous instruction to a patient reads as a curt order.
creator_notes: Scheduling only; deliberately contains no medical content. Minimal pair partner of HIN_POL_007. Not yet reviewed by a native speaker.

context.text: Kal aa jaun kya?

source_utterance.text: Haan tu gyarah baje aa ja.

literal_gloss: Yes, you come at eleven o'clock.
context_explanation: The friend's question establishes that this is an agreement to a proposed visit, and the intimate 'tu' form marks a close friendship.
preservation_requirement: The translation must sound like warm, casual agreement between close friends. The intimate 'tu' register must not be inflated into polite or formal English. This is the familiar half of a minimal pair with HIN_POL_006.
reference_translations: Yeah, come over at eleven.
acceptable_variants: Sure, come round at eleven.
contrastive_translation: Yes, please arrive at eleven o'clock.
contrastive_error: The contrastive translation keeps the scheduling content but replaces intimate 'tu' register with polite, formal English, implying a distance between close friends that the source does not encode.
creator_notes: The 'tu' form is intimate rather than rude here because the addressee is a close friend; native reviewers should confirm this reading holds across regions. Minimal pair partner of HIN_POL_006.

context.text: Main chahta hoon ki yeh kaam aaj hi poora ho jaye.

source_utterance.text: Sir, koshish karta hoon, lekin thoda mushkil lag raha hai.

literal_gloss: Sir, I will try, but it is looking a little difficult.
context_explanation: Without the manager's demand this reads as a neutral remark about difficulty. In context it is a face-saving, hedged pushback against an instruction from a superior.
preservation_requirement: The translation must preserve the hedge. The employee is signalling difficulty without refusing outright, and must not be made to reject the manager's instruction.
reference_translations: I'll try, sir, but it does look a bit difficult.
acceptable_variants: I'll do my best, sir, though it seems a little difficult.
contrastive_translation: I'll try, sir, but that's not going to happen.
contrastive_error: The contrastive translation keeps the surface concession but converts the deliberately vague hedge 'thoda mushkil lag raha hai' into a flat prediction of failure, which reads as an employee contradicting a manager outright.
creator_notes: Marked CRITICAL because the contrastive reading could plausibly damage a workplace relationship. Native reviewers should confirm the severity assignment.

context.text: Kal ka presentation ready hai?

source_utterance.text: Sir almost done hai, bas ek slide baaki hai.

literal_gloss: Sir, it is almost done, only one slide is left.
context_explanation: The manager's question establishes what 'almost done' refers to. The English words here are ordinary workplace borrowings and carry no separate discourse function.
preservation_requirement: The translation must preserve the deference an intern shows a manager, which is carried almost entirely by the address term 'Sir'.
reference_translations: It's almost done, sir — just one slide left.
acceptable_variants: Almost finished, sir, only one slide to go.
contrastive_translation: It's almost done, just one slide left.
contrastive_error: The contrastive translation is semantically complete but drops the address term 'Sir', which is the only marker of the status difference between an intern and a manager.
creator_notes: Deliberately labelled code_switch_function NOT_APPLICABLE: 'presentation', 'ready', 'almost done' and 'slide' are unmarked borrowings, not pragmatically loaded switches. This item tests that annotators do not over-read code-mixing.

source_utterance.text: Bhaiya, thoda discount kar dijiye na.

literal_gloss: Brother, please give a little discount.
context_explanation: No previous turn is needed. The address term 'bhaiya' and the coaxing particle 'na' establish the bargaining register within the utterance, and the request names its own object.
preservation_requirement: The translation must preserve the friendly, coaxing register of ordinary bargaining. The kinship address term 'bhaiya' and the softener 'na' make this a warm appeal rather than a demand.
reference_translations: Come on, brother, give me a bit of a discount.
acceptable_variants: Bhaiya, do give me a little discount.
contrastive_translation: Give me a discount.
contrastive_error: The contrastive translation keeps the request content but removes the fictive-kinship address term and the coaxing particle 'na', turning warm, conventional bargaining into a bare demand.
creator_notes: A context-independent item: the utterance is fully interpretable on its own. Whether 'bhaiya' should be kept untranslated is a translation decision native reviewers should rule on.

context.text: Aap log deadline extend karne ki request kar rahe the?

source_utterance.text: Ji sir, agar possible ho toh do din extra mil jayein.

literal_gloss: Yes sir, if it is possible then we may get two extra days.
context_explanation: The professor's question establishes what is being requested, so the student's turn can be read as a hedged confirmation of that request.
preservation_requirement: The translation must preserve the heavy hedging. The student is leaving the professor room to refuse and must not be made to issue an instruction. This is the deferential half of a minimal pair with HNG_POL_004.
reference_translations: Yes sir — if it's possible, it would really help to have two extra days.
acceptable_variants: Yes sir, if it could be possible, perhaps two extra days?
contrastive_translation: Yes sir, if possible give us two extra days.
contrastive_error: The contrastive translation keeps the conditional 'if possible' but converts the impersonal 'mil jayein' construction into a direct imperative, so a hedged appeal becomes an instruction to a professor.
creator_notes: Minimal pair partner of HNG_POL_004, which expresses the same request between classmates. Not yet reviewed by a native speaker.

context.text: Tu extension maang raha hai kya?

source_utterance.text: Haan yaar, do din extra mil jaye toh ho jayega.

literal_gloss: Yes friend, if two extra days are obtained then it will get done.
context_explanation: The classmate's question establishes the topic of the extension, and the 'tu' form marks the two speakers as close peers.
preservation_requirement: The translation must stay in a casual peer register. It must not be rendered in institutional or bureaucratic English. This is the casual half of a minimal pair with HNG_POL_003.
reference_translations: Yeah man, if we get two extra days we'll be fine.
acceptable_variants: Yeah, a couple of extra days and it's done.
contrastive_translation: Yes, if we are granted two additional days it will be completed.
contrastive_error: The contrastive translation preserves the propositional content but replaces casual peer register and the solidarity marker 'yaar' with formal, institutional English, implying distance between close classmates.
creator_notes: Minimal pair partner of HNG_POL_003. Tests the over-formalisation direction of failure. Not yet reviewed by a native speaker.

context.text: Kal hamare ghar dinner pe aa jao.
Ji, zaroor.

source_utterance.text: Toh phir saat baje aa jana.

literal_gloss: Then come at seven o'clock.
context_explanation: Without the invitation and its acceptance, this reads as a bare instruction. In context it is the warm closing of an invitation from an elder relative, not an order.
preservation_requirement: The translation must read as the friendly settling of an agreed invitation, not as a command issued to the niece.
reference_translations: Come over at seven, then.
acceptable_variants: All right, see you at seven.
contrastive_translation: Then you must arrive at seven o'clock.
contrastive_error: The contrastive translation keeps the time and the invitation content but adds obligation, turning an elder's warm closing of an accepted invitation into a requirement imposed on the niece.
creator_notes: Two context turns, including an acceptance turn, which is what makes the final turn a warm closing rather than an initial request.

context.text: Kitna garam ho raha hai aaj.

source_utterance.text: Haan, pankha band hi hai shayad.

literal_gloss: Yes, the fan is probably switched off.
context_explanation: Without the complaint about the heat, this is a bare observation about a fan. In context it is a hint that the listener should switch the fan on.
preservation_requirement: The translation must remain an observation that merely implies the request. Making the request explicit destroys the phenomenon the item is built to test.
reference_translations: Yeah, I think the fan's been left off.
acceptable_variants: Yeah, the fan's probably switched off.
contrastive_translation: Yes, turn the fan on.
contrastive_error: The contrastive translation states the implied request outright. The propositional content is closely related, but a deliberately indirect hint becomes a direct imperative.
creator_notes: A canonical over-explicitation failure: the system resolves the implicature for the reader rather than leaving it implied.

context.text: Weekend pe office aa sakte ho?

source_utterance.text: Sir, weekend pe ghar pe kuch program hai.

literal_gloss: Sir, there is some function at home on the weekend.
context_explanation: Without the manager's question this is a neutral statement about a family event. In context it is a refusal that is deliberately never stated as one.
preservation_requirement: The translation must leave the refusal implied. The employee is avoiding an explicit 'no' to a superior, and the translation must preserve that avoidance. This is the indirect half of a minimal pair with HIN_IND_004.
reference_translations: Sir, there's a family function at home this weekend.
acceptable_variants: I've got something on at home this weekend, sir.
contrastive_translation: Sir, I can't come on the weekend.
contrastive_error: The contrastive translation converts an implied refusal into an explicit one. It remains polite, but it removes the face-saving indirectness that the employee deliberately used with a superior.
creator_notes: Minimal pair partner of HIN_IND_004, which performs the same refusal directly between friends. Not yet reviewed by a native speaker.

context.text: Weekend pe aa sakta hai?

source_utterance.text: Nahi yaar, nahi aa paunga.

literal_gloss: No friend, I will not be able to come.
context_explanation: The friend's question establishes what is being refused. The close friendship is what licenses an unhedged refusal without causing offence.
preservation_requirement: The translation must remain a clear, unambiguous refusal. Softening it would leave the listener uncertain whether the speaker is coming. This is the direct half of a minimal pair with HIN_IND_003.
reference_translations: No man, I won't be able to make it.
acceptable_variants: Nah, I can't come.
contrastive_translation: I might have something on that weekend.
contrastive_error: The contrastive translation replaces a clear refusal with a vague hedge, so the listener could reasonably still expect the speaker to attend. The propositional content is close but the illocutionary force is lost.
creator_notes: Deliberately tests the opposite failure direction from HIN_IND_003: here the error is adding indirectness that the source does not have.

context.text: Sir, report ho gayi hai.

source_utterance.text: Achha, isme references thode kam lag rahe hain.

literal_gloss: I see, the references in this seem a little few.
context_explanation: Without the student's announcement that the report is finished, this is a neutral observation. In context it is a softened instruction to add more references.
preservation_requirement: The translation must keep the criticism softened and implicit. The professor is choosing not to issue a direct order, and the translation must not supply one.
reference_translations: I see — the references here look a little thin.
acceptable_variants: Right, the reference list seems a bit short.
contrastive_translation: I see. Add more references.
contrastive_error: The contrastive translation converts a deliberately softened, face-saving criticism into a bare imperative, changing how much the professor is imposing on the student.
creator_notes: Status is reversed relative to most POL items: here the higher-status speaker is the one choosing indirectness.

context.text: Bhaiya, yeh thoda sasta nahi ho sakta?

source_utterance.text: Sahab, rate toh fixed hi hai.

literal_gloss: Sir, the rate is fixed.
context_explanation: Without the customer's request for a lower price this is a neutral statement of policy. In context it is a refusal to bargain, phrased impersonally to avoid confrontation.
preservation_requirement: The translation must keep the refusal impersonal. Attributing the refusal to the shopkeeper personally rather than to the fixed price makes it more confrontational than intended.
reference_translations: Sir, the price is fixed, I'm afraid.
acceptable_variants: The rate is fixed, sir.
contrastive_translation: No, I won't lower it.
contrastive_error: The contrastive translation preserves the refusal but re-frames it as the shopkeeper's personal decision rather than an impersonal fact about the price, and drops the address term, making an ordinary bargaining exchange confrontational.
creator_notes: The impersonal 'rate toh fixed hi hai' construction is the politeness strategy under test. Native reviewers should confirm 'sahab' reads as ordinary shopkeeper courtesy here.

context.text: Namaste, mujhe doctor sahab se milna tha.
Woh char baje tak free nahin hain.

source_utterance.text: Mujhe paanch baje tak nikalna hai...

literal_gloss: I have to leave by five o'clock...
context_explanation: Without the receptionist's statement that no slot is free until four, this is a bare remark about the speaker's schedule. In context it is an implied request for an earlier appointment.
preservation_requirement: The translation must leave the request implied and preserve the trailing, unfinished quality of the utterance. Stating the request outright removes the phenomenon under test.
reference_translations: I do have to leave by five, though...
acceptable_variants: The thing is, I need to leave by five...
contrastive_translation: I have to leave by five, so give me an earlier slot.
contrastive_error: The contrastive translation spells out the request that the speaker deliberately left implicit, converting a tentative hint into an explicit demand on the receptionist.
creator_notes: Scheduling only; contains no medical content. The trailing ellipsis carries part of the indirectness and should be preserved in translation.

context.text: Yaar, thode paise udhaar mil sakte hain?

source_utterance.text: Abhi toh khud thoda tight chal raha hoon.

literal_gloss: Right now I myself am running a little tight.
context_explanation: Without the request this is a passing remark about the speaker's finances. In context it is an embarrassed refusal that avoids saying no to a friend.
preservation_requirement: The translation must preserve the embarrassed deflection. The speaker is protecting both his own face and his friend's, and must not be made to refuse bluntly.
reference_translations: Things are a bit tight for me right now, honestly.
acceptable_variants: I'm running a little short myself at the moment.
contrastive_translation: I'm not lending you money right now.
contrastive_error: The contrastive translation converts an embarrassed, face-saving deflection into an explicit refusal to lend, which between close friends is markedly more wounding than what the speaker said.
creator_notes: Marked CRITICAL because the contrastive reading could cause real offence between friends. Severity is a judgement the native reviewers should confirm.

context.text: Kal ka session tum handle kar loge?

source_utterance.text: Sir main try karta hoon, but kal mera ek personal commitment bhi hai.

literal_gloss: Sir I will try, but tomorrow I also have a personal commitment.
context_explanation: Without the manager's request this is a neutral statement about the speaker's schedule. In context the mention of a personal commitment is what performs the refusal.
preservation_requirement: The translation must keep the refusal implied behind a stated willingness to try. The employee is avoiding an explicit no to a manager.
reference_translations: I'll try, sir, but I do have a personal commitment tomorrow.
acceptable_variants: I'll see what I can do, sir, though I have something personal on tomorrow.
contrastive_translation: I'll try, sir, but I can't do it tomorrow.
contrastive_error: The contrastive translation keeps the offer to try but replaces the oblique mention of a commitment with an explicit statement of inability, removing the face-saving indirectness.
creator_notes: The English tokens ('try', 'but', 'personal commitment') are unmarked workplace borrowings, so code_switch_function is NOT_APPLICABLE.

context.text: Kal ka lecture miss ho gaya mera.

source_utterance.text: Mere paas notes hain, agar chahiye toh.

literal_gloss: I have the notes, if they are wanted.
context_explanation: The classmate's remark about missing the lecture establishes why the notes are relevant and makes the utterance readable as an offer.
preservation_requirement: The translation must keep the offer low-pressure. The trailing conditional 'agar chahiye toh' leaves the classmate free to decline without awkwardness.
reference_translations: I've got the notes, if you want them.
acceptable_variants: I have the notes — if you need them, that is.
contrastive_translation: I have the notes. Take them.
contrastive_error: The contrastive translation keeps the propositional content but drops the conditional that made the offer optional, so a low-pressure offer becomes an instruction that removes the classmate's freedom to decline.
creator_notes: Severity is MINOR because the helpful intent still comes through even though the offer is mis-framed as a directive.

context.text: Mujhe yeh order urgent chahiye.
Aaj hi delivery ho sakti hai kya?

source_utterance.text: Ma'am aaj toh thoda difficult hoga, kal try karte hain.

literal_gloss: Ma'am, today it will be a little difficult, we will try tomorrow.
context_explanation: The two customer turns establish the urgency and the specific request, which is what makes the agent's hedged reply a refusal rather than a neutral scheduling remark.
preservation_requirement: The translation must keep the refusal softened. 'Thoda difficult' is a hedge that avoids telling a customer flatly that their request is impossible. This is the hedged half of a minimal pair with HNG_IND_004.
reference_translations: That'll be a bit difficult today, ma'am — we'll try for tomorrow.
acceptable_variants: Today might be tricky, ma'am; let's try tomorrow.
contrastive_translation: That's not possible today, ma'am. We'll do it tomorrow.
contrastive_error: The contrastive translation replaces the hedge 'thoda difficult' with a flat statement of impossibility, so a softened service refusal becomes a blunt denial to a customer.
creator_notes: Minimal pair partner of HNG_IND_004, which performs the same refusal directly in a peer register. Not yet reviewed by a native speaker.

context.text: Aaj hi ho jayega kya?

source_utterance.text: Nahi yaar, aaj toh impossible hai.

literal_gloss: No friend, today it is impossible.
context_explanation: The friend's question establishes what is being refused. The close friendship licenses an unhedged refusal.
preservation_requirement: The translation must remain a clear refusal in a casual register. Hedging it would leave the friend uncertain. This is the direct half of a minimal pair with HNG_IND_003.
reference_translations: No man, today's impossible.
acceptable_variants: Nah, no chance today.
contrastive_translation: It may be somewhat difficult today.
contrastive_error: The contrastive translation replaces an unambiguous refusal with a tentative hedge, so the friend could still expect the thing to happen. It also shifts a casual peer register into cautious formal English.
creator_notes: Deliberately the inverse failure of HNG_IND_003: indirectness added rather than removed.

context.text: Main aaj phir late ho gaya.

source_utterance.text: Tumse toh yahi ummeed thi.

literal_gloss: This was exactly the expectation from you.
context_explanation: Without the friend's self-deprecating admission of being late, the utterance could be read as a genuine reproach. The admission is what marks it as affectionate teasing.
preservation_requirement: The translation must preserve affectionate teasing between close friends. It must not become contempt or a genuine insult.
reference_translations: Ha, that's exactly what I'd expect from you.
acceptable_variants: Of course — classic you.
contrastive_translation: That's exactly what I expect from someone like you.
contrastive_error: The contrastive translation is semantically very close but 'someone like you' introduces categorical contempt, turning warm teasing between friends into a put-down.
creator_notes: Marked CRITICAL because the contrastive version reverses the social meaning from solidarity to insult. Teasing and insult are the hardest boundary in this category and native reviewers should scrutinise it.

context.text: Maa, main khana nahi khaunga aaj.

source_utterance.text: Kyun beta, tabiyat theek hai na?

literal_gloss: Why child, your health is fine, isn't it?
context_explanation: The son's refusal of food establishes what prompts the mother's concern and makes the question read as care rather than interrogation.
preservation_requirement: The translation must preserve maternal concern. The endearment 'beta' and the tag 'na' soften the question into an expression of worry.
reference_translations: Why, beta — are you feeling all right?
acceptable_variants: What's wrong, son, are you feeling okay?
contrastive_translation: Why? Is there something wrong with you?
contrastive_error: The contrastive translation asks about the same thing but drops the endearment and the softening tag, so maternal concern reads as suspicion or irritation directed at the son.
creator_notes: Whether 'beta' should be kept untranslated or rendered as 'son' is a translation decision for native reviewers.

context.text: Yeh file abhi tak nahi bheji?

source_utterance.text: Bhej di thi maine, dobara dekh lijiye.

literal_gloss: I had sent it, please look again.
context_explanation: The accusatory question is what makes the reply a restrained correction. Without it the utterance is a neutral statement about a file.
preservation_requirement: The translation must preserve restrained irritation: the speaker is annoyed but is deliberately staying polite with a colleague. This is the restrained half of a minimal pair with HIN_STA_004.
reference_translations: I did send it — could you check again, please?
acceptable_variants: I had sent it; please do have another look.
contrastive_translation: I sent it. Check again.
contrastive_error: The contrastive translation keeps the content but drops the respectful 'dekh lijiye' form, so controlled irritation that was being held in check reads as open rudeness to a colleague.
creator_notes: Minimal pair partner of HIN_STA_004, in which the same speaker lets the irritation show openly. The pair isolates how much politeness work the 'lijiye' form is doing.

context.text: Yeh file abhi tak nahi bheji?

source_utterance.text: Kitni baar bhejun main?

literal_gloss: How many times should I send it?
context_explanation: The accusatory question is what makes this a rhetorical protest rather than a genuine request for instructions.
preservation_requirement: The translation must preserve open frustration and the rhetorical nature of the question. It must not be flattened into cheerful compliance or a literal request for a number. This is the openly irritated half of a minimal pair with HIN_STA_003.
reference_translations: How many times am I supposed to send it?
acceptable_variants: How many more times do I have to send it?
contrastive_translation: I'd be happy to send it again.
contrastive_error: The contrastive translation refers to the same action but erases the frustration entirely and replaces a rhetorical protest with cheerful willingness, reversing the speaker's attitude.
creator_notes: Minimal pair partner of HIN_STA_003. Tests whether rhetorical questions survive as protests rather than being read literally.

context.text: Sir, mujhse ek galti ho gayi report mein.
Maine theek kar di hai, par thodi der ho gayi.

source_utterance.text: Koi baat nahi, ho jata hai.

literal_gloss: It is no matter, it happens.
context_explanation: The junior's admission of a mistake is what makes this reassurance rather than indifference. Without it, 'it happens' has no target.
preservation_requirement: The translation must read as warm reassurance from a senior to a worried junior. It must not sound like the senior is brushing the junior off.
reference_translations: Don't worry about it — these things happen.
acceptable_variants: It's all right, it happens to everyone.
contrastive_translation: It doesn't matter. It happens.
contrastive_error: The contrastive translation is a close literal rendering but flattens warm reassurance into indifference, so the junior may read it as being dismissed rather than comforted.
creator_notes: 'Koi baat nahi' is highly conventionalised; a literal rendering loses its reassuring force. Two context turns.

context.text: Maine poora syllabus ek din mein khatam kar liya.

source_utterance.text: Achha? Poora?

literal_gloss: Really? All of it?
context_explanation: The implausible claim in the previous turn is what makes the short question read as disbelief rather than as a neutral request for confirmation.
preservation_requirement: The translation must preserve the speaker's open scepticism. Rendering it as admiration reverses the attitude entirely.
reference_translations: Oh really? The whole thing?
acceptable_variants: Seriously? All of it?
contrastive_translation: Oh nice! All of it?
contrastive_error: The contrastive translation keeps the question but replaces disbelief with genuine admiration, reversing the speaker's stance toward the classmate's claim.
creator_notes: Very short utterance where nearly all pragmatic content is contextual. Relevant to the finding that short turns benefit most from context in evaluation (Agrawal et al. 2024).

context.text: Maine gym join kar liya.

source_utterance.text: Wow, kitne din chalega yeh motivation?

literal_gloss: Wow, how many days will this motivation last?
context_explanation: The friend's announcement is what the teasing targets. Without it the question about motivation has no referent.
preservation_requirement: The translation must preserve friendly teasing between close friends. It must not become a genuine prediction of failure.
reference_translations: Ha, and how long is this motivation going to last?
acceptable_variants: Nice — so how long before this motivation dies?
contrastive_translation: Great. I'm sure you'll give up in a few days.
contrastive_error: The contrastive translation makes the teasing implicature explicit and asserts it as a prediction, converting light banter into a sincere put-down.
creator_notes: 'gym', 'join', 'wow' and 'motivation' are unmarked borrowings, hence code_switch_function NOT_APPLICABLE. The teasing lives in the rhetorical question, not the switch.

context.text: Yeh report phir se banani padegi.

source_utterance.text: Sir, main teen baar already revise kar chuka hoon.

literal_gloss: Sir, I have already revised it three times.
context_explanation: The manager's instruction to redo the report is what turns a factual statement about revisions into a restrained protest against it.
preservation_requirement: The translation must preserve the implied protest. The employee is pushing back while staying respectful, and must not be made to simply agree.
reference_translations: Sir, I've already revised it three times.
acceptable_variants: I have revised it three times already, sir.
contrastive_translation: Sure sir, I've revised it three times.
contrastive_error: The contrastive translation adds a token of agreement that erases the protest, turning restrained frustration into willing compliance with the manager's instruction.
creator_notes: The stance is carried by the bare assertion in a context where agreement was expected. Native reviewers should confirm the protest reading.

context.text: Interview thoda kharab gaya.

source_utterance.text: Arre, ek interview se kya hota hai yaar.

literal_gloss: Oh, what happens from one interview, friend.
context_explanation: The junior's disappointment is what makes this encouragement. Without it the rhetorical question reads as dismissing the importance of interviews in general.
preservation_requirement: The translation must preserve warm encouragement. The rhetorical question is minimising the setback to comfort the listener, not belittling the listener's feelings.
reference_translations: Come on, one interview doesn't decide anything.
acceptable_variants: Hey, it's just one interview, yaar.
contrastive_translation: So what? It's just one interview.
contrastive_error: The contrastive translation keeps the minimising content but 'so what' redirects the dismissal at the listener's feelings, so warm encouragement reads as impatience with the junior's disappointment.
creator_notes: The discourse particle 'arre' and the solidarity marker 'yaar' carry the warmth; both are easy to drop in translation.

context.text: Tu kal aaya hi nahi.

source_utterance.text: Yaar sorry, bilkul bhool gaya tha.

literal_gloss: Friend, sorry, I had completely forgotten.
context_explanation: The friend's reproach establishes what is being apologised for and makes the embarrassment legible.
preservation_requirement: The translation must preserve a genuinely embarrassed apology between close friends, not a routine or perfunctory one.
reference_translations: Sorry man, I completely forgot.
acceptable_variants: Ah sorry yaar, it totally slipped my mind.
contrastive_translation: Sorry, it slipped my mind.
contrastive_error: The contrastive translation keeps the apology but drops the solidarity marker and the intensifier 'bilkul', so a visibly embarrassed apology between close friends becomes a routine, slightly distant excuse.
creator_notes: Severity is MINOR: the apology still lands, but its emotional weight is reduced. Useful as a low-severity calibration point for annotators.

context.text: Sir, thoda time aur mil sakta hai?
Pehle bhi do baar extend kiya hai.

source_utterance.text: Dekho, this is the final deadline. Iske baad extension nahi milega.

literal_gloss: Look, this is the final deadline. After this no extension will be given.
context_explanation: The request and the manager's reminder of two previous extensions establish why the manager shifts into English: the switch marks the deadline as an official, non-negotiable position rather than a personal opinion.
preservation_requirement: The translation must preserve the shift into an official, institutional footing. The deadline statement must read as final and non-negotiable, not as a personal view.
reference_translations: Look — this is the final deadline. There'll be no extension after this.
acceptable_variants: Listen, this is the final deadline; no extensions after this.
contrastive_translation: Look, I think this is probably the last deadline, no extension after that.
contrastive_error: The contrastive translation preserves the propositional content but adds hedging ('I think', 'probably'), converting the authoritative, official register signalled by the switch into English into a tentative personal opinion.
creator_notes: The switch into English here is the AUTHORITY function: institutional English marks the utterance as policy. Because the whole item is translated into English, the challenge is preserving the footing shift without the surface switch. Native reviewers should assess whether this is testable in an English target.

context.text: Result aa gaya?

source_utterance.text: Haan yaar, I got selected! Mujhe abhi tak yakeen nahi ho raha.

literal_gloss: Yes friend, I got selected! I still cannot believe it.
context_explanation: The friend's question establishes what the result refers to, though the excitement is legible from the utterance alone.
preservation_requirement: The translation must preserve the excitement that the switch into English carries. A flat, neutral report of the outcome loses the emotional peak of the turn.
reference_translations: Yes! I got selected — I still can't believe it.
acceptable_variants: Yeah man, I got in! I still can't believe it.
contrastive_translation: Yes, I was selected. I still cannot believe it.
contrastive_error: The contrastive translation is semantically equivalent but the shift to a passive, formal register erases the emotional intensity that the code switch and the exclamation carry.
creator_notes: The English clause is the emotional peak of the turn, surrounded by Hindi. Tests whether register flattening is detected as a pragmatic loss.

context.text: Yeh error kyun aa raha hai?

source_utterance.text: Tumne array ka index galat diya hai, isliye out of bounds ja raha hai.

literal_gloss: You have given the array's index wrongly, that is why it is going out of bounds.
context_explanation: The student's question establishes the debugging setting, which is what makes the English terms ordinary technical vocabulary rather than marked switches.
preservation_requirement: The translation must render the English technical terms as plain, unmarked vocabulary. It must not add emphasis or attitude that the speaker did not express.
reference_translations: You've given the wrong array index, so it's going out of bounds.
acceptable_variants: The array index you gave is wrong, which is why it goes out of bounds.
contrastive_translation: You've given the wrong so-called 'array index', so it's going 'out of bounds'.
contrastive_error: The contrastive translation treats routine technical borrowing as marked usage by adding 'so-called' and scare quotes, which imports a sceptical, faintly mocking attitude toward the student's vocabulary that the source does not encode.
creator_notes: Included deliberately as a negative control for the code-switching category: it tests that annotators and systems do not over-read every English token as pragmatically loaded. The contrastive fails by treating unmarked technical borrowing as if it were a marked switch.

context.text: Everything okay? Meeting mein tum kaafi quiet the.

source_utterance.text: Arre kuch nahi yaar, bas thoda ghar ki tension hai.

literal_gloss: Oh nothing friend, just a little tension at home.
context_explanation: The colleague opens in workplace English. The reply switches into Hindi, and that shift is what signals a move from professional to personal footing. Without the English opener the switch is invisible.
preservation_requirement: The translation must preserve the move into a closer, more personal register. The reply should read as confiding in a friend, not as a formal answer to a workplace enquiry.
reference_translations: Ah, it's nothing, yaar — just some stuff going on at home.
acceptable_variants: Oh, it's nothing really, just a bit of family stuff.
contrastive_translation: It is nothing. There is simply some tension at home.
contrastive_error: The contrastive translation keeps the propositional content but removes the discourse particles and the shift into intimacy, so a confiding reply to a friendly enquiry becomes a distant, formal answer.
creator_notes: Requires the English-language context turn to make the switch legible; a strong test of context dependence. Whether 'yaar' should be retained untranslated is a decision for native reviewers.

context.text: Maine assignment aaj subah shuru kiya tha.
Aur ab submit bhi kar diya.

source_utterance.text: Wah, what a genius. Hum toh kya hi kar sakte hain.

literal_gloss: Wow, what a genius. What can we even do.
context_explanation: The classmate's boast in the two previous turns is what marks the English praise as ironic. Read alone, 'what a genius' is sincere admiration.
preservation_requirement: The translation must preserve the ironic reading. Rendering the praise literally reverses the speaker's attitude toward the classmate's boast.
reference_translations: Oh wow, what a genius — what hope do the rest of us have?
acceptable_variants: Ah, what a genius. The rest of us may as well give up.
contrastive_translation: Wow, what a genius. There's nothing we can do.
contrastive_error: The contrastive translation reads the sarcastic praise literally and renders the second clause as sincere resignation, so mock admiration between friends becomes genuine admiration and defeat.
creator_notes: The switch into English carries the sarcasm; the Hindi clause supplies the mock self-deprecation. Sarcasm is acknowledged in the blueprint as hard to validate, so this item needs particular scrutiny from native reviewers.

context.text: Manager ne kya kaha?

source_utterance.text: Usne bola, 'this is not acceptable', aur chala gaya.

literal_gloss: He said, 'this is not acceptable', and left.
context_explanation: The colleague's question establishes that the speaker is reporting what the manager said, which supports the quotative reading of the English clause.
preservation_requirement: The translation must keep the English clause marked as the manager's own words. Converting it to indirect speech loses the fact that the speaker is reproducing the manager's exact phrasing.
reference_translations: He said, 'this is not acceptable', and walked off.
acceptable_variants: He goes, 'this is not acceptable', and just left.
contrastive_translation: He said it was not acceptable and left.
contrastive_error: The contrastive translation converts a verbatim quotation into indirect reported speech. The propositional content survives, but the speaker is no longer reproducing the manager's exact words, which is what the switch marked.
creator_notes: Severity is MINOR because the reported content is preserved and only the quotative framing is lost. Provides a low-severity calibration point within the code-switching category.

source_utterance.text: Aunty ji, aap yahan baith jaiye.

literal_gloss: Aunty, you please sit here.
context_explanation: No previous turn is needed. The honorific address 'Aunty ji', the respectful pronoun 'aap' and the '-iye' imperative carry the deference entirely within the utterance, and 'yahan' is resolved by the physical setting rather than by prior discourse.
preservation_requirement: The translation must preserve a young stranger offering a seat deferentially to an elder. The respectful imperative must not become a bare instruction.
reference_translations: Please, aunty, do sit here.
acceptable_variants: Aunty ji, please take this seat.
contrastive_translation: Aunty, sit here.
contrastive_error: The contrastive translation keeps the offer but renders the honorific imperative 'baith jaiye' as a bare imperative and drops the '-ji' suffix, so a deferential offer to an elderly stranger reads as the speaker instructing her.
creator_notes: Deliberately context-independent: a control item whose pragmatic load is carried entirely by Hindi honorific morphology rather than by preceding turns. Added to strengthen the NOT_REQUIRED control group (pilot_issues.md issue 1).

source_utterance.text: Namaste sir, main aapki kya help kar sakta hoon?

literal_gloss: Greetings sir, what help can I do for you?
context_explanation: No previous turn is needed. This is a call-opening formula: the greeting, the address term and the 'aap' construction mark the service register completely on their own, and nothing in the utterance refers back to earlier discourse.
preservation_requirement: The translation must preserve a courteous, formal service opening. It must not become a brusque enquiry about what the customer wants.
reference_translations: Hello sir, how may I help you?
acceptable_variants: Good day sir, how can I help you today?
contrastive_translation: Hi, what do you want?
contrastive_error: The contrastive translation asks the same thing but replaces the formal greeting and offer of assistance with a casual opener and a blunt demand, so a courteous service greeting reads as impatience with the customer.
creator_notes: Context-independent control item. 'help' is an unmarked borrowing, hence code_switch_function NOT_APPLICABLE. Added for the NOT_REQUIRED control group (pilot_issues.md issue 1).

source_utterance.text: Kya aap khidki band kar sakte hain?

literal_gloss: Can you close the window?
context_explanation: No previous turn is needed. This is a conventionally indirect request: a question about the listener's ability is understood as a request by convention, independently of any preceding discourse, and 'khidki' names its own referent.
preservation_requirement: The translation must remain a polite request. It must not be rendered as a literal enquiry about whether the listener is physically capable of closing the window.
reference_translations: Could you close the window, please?
acceptable_variants: Would you mind closing the window?
contrastive_translation: Are you able to close the window?
contrastive_error: The contrastive translation reads the conventionally indirect request literally, as a question about the listener's physical capability. The propositional content is nearly identical, but the utterance stops functioning as a request and, addressed to a stranger, can read as pointed or patronising.
creator_notes: Context-independent control item, and a classic conventional-indirectness case: the request force is conventional rather than contextual, which is exactly why no previous turn is needed. Added for the NOT_REQUIRED control group (pilot_issues.md issue 1).

source_utterance.text: Is report par thoda aur mehnat karni padegi.

literal_gloss: A little more effort will have to be put on this report.
context_explanation: No previous turn is needed. The impersonal construction 'mehnat karni padegi' names no agent, and the report is named in the utterance itself, so the softened, face-saving quality of the criticism is fully recoverable on its own.
preservation_requirement: The translation must keep the criticism impersonal. Naming the student as the one who fell short makes it markedly more face-threatening than what was said.
reference_translations: This report will need a bit more work.
acceptable_variants: A little more work is needed on this report.
contrastive_translation: You didn't work hard enough on this report.
contrastive_error: The contrastive translation preserves the assessment but reassigns it to the student personally, converting an agentless, face-saving criticism into a direct accusation from a professor.
creator_notes: Context-independent control item. The politeness work is done by the agentless 'padegi' construction, which survives without any preceding turn. Added for the NOT_REQUIRED control group (pilot_issues.md issue 1).

source_utterance.text: Arre, apna khayal rakha karo thoda.

literal_gloss: Oh, do take care of yourself a little.
context_explanation: No previous turn is needed. The particle 'arre', the habitual 'rakha karo' form and the softener 'thoda' mark affectionate concern within the utterance, and nothing in it refers back to earlier discourse.
preservation_requirement: The translation must preserve affectionate concern between close friends. It must not become a reproach about the listener's habits.
reference_translations: Hey, do look after yourself a bit.
acceptable_variants: Come on, take a bit of care of yourself.
contrastive_translation: You should take better care of yourself.
contrastive_error: The contrastive translation gives the same advice but the comparative 'better' implies the listener has been failing to do so, turning warm concern into a mild reproach.
creator_notes: Context-independent control item. The warmth is carried by discourse particles rather than by context. Added for the NOT_REQUIRED control group (pilot_issues.md issue 1).

source_utterance.text: Yaar tension mat lo, sab theek ho jayega.

literal_gloss: Friend, don't take tension, everything will become fine.
context_explanation: No previous turn is needed. 'Sab theek ho jayega' is a general reassurance formula rather than a reference to any specific prior topic, and the solidarity marker 'yaar' establishes the closeness on its own.
preservation_requirement: The translation must preserve warm, casual reassurance between close friends. It must not become a flat or impersonal formula.
reference_translations: Don't stress, man — it'll all be fine.
acceptable_variants: Chill yaar, everything will work out.
contrastive_translation: Do not worry. Everything will be fine.
contrastive_error: The contrastive translation reassures about the same thing but drops the solidarity marker and shifts into a clipped, formal register, so warmth between close friends becomes an impersonal formula that could come from a stranger.
creator_notes: Context-independent control item. Severity is MINOR because the reassurance still lands and only its warmth is reduced; this also provides a low-severity calibration point. 'tension' is an unmarked borrowing. Added for the NOT_REQUIRED control group (pilot_issues.md issue 1).

source_utterance.text: Aaj se ek rule hai — no phones during meetings.

literal_gloss: From today there is one rule — no phones during meetings.
context_explanation: No previous turn is needed. The switch into clipped institutional English for the rule itself marks it as official policy rather than personal preference, and that contrast is visible within the single utterance because the Hindi frame surrounds it.
preservation_requirement: The translation must preserve the rule as official and non-negotiable. It must not be softened into the manager's personal preference.
reference_translations: From today there's a rule — no phones during meetings.
acceptable_variants: There's a new rule from today: no phones during meetings.
contrastive_translation: From today I'd prefer it if people didn't use phones in meetings.
contrastive_error: The contrastive translation conveys the same restriction but reframes it as the manager's personal preference, losing the institutional authority that the switch into formal English marked and leaving the rule apparently negotiable.
creator_notes: Context-independent control item, and the only code-switching item that does not depend on a preceding turn: the Hindi frame and the English rule sit inside one utterance, so the contrast is self-contained. Relevant to the open question of whether the code-switching category is testable with an English target (pilot_issues.md issue 4).
